task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: PULL_UP as a counter play type
unit-level consistency (share of units with lift>0, median lift)
regression to the mean and selection on a low-PPP state
placebo and alternative counter play types
methodological_questions: What is a 'unit' (team-season, team-game, player), and what is the minimum exposure per unit?
How is 'PNR fail' defined from play-by-play without using the outcome of the possessions that are later scored (outcome-derived label, leakage)?
What is lift measured against: PULL_UP PPP in non-fail states, PULL_UP share, or other counter play types in the same state?
Is the 70% / 2pp rule calibrated to the sampling noise of per-unit lift (power, null distribution)?
Does the selection on a low-PNR-PPP state mechanically create positive lift for any subsequent play type (RTM, mechanical floor)?
Is the effect stable across seasons and between regular season and playoffs?
How is confounding by team, player, opponent, score and clock handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Falsification of the 'A1 adapter PPP lift is real coverage response'. Wrong-way teams (dPPP +0.0111, n=274) did not do worse than no-signal teams (+0.1260, n=57). The adapter-minus-no-signal gap was negative (-0.0361 with 1 vote, -0.1170 with 2 votes). The carryover test was not significant (p=0.842). Recorded mechanism: C_artifact (apparent effect produced by a construction, selection or labelling flaw). Recorded limits: label/classification error and selection/regression to the mean. Recorded risks: LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR.

Within-scheme re-test controlling early-third PPP selection. Adapter-vs-wrong-way gap: DROP +0.0830 (Welch p=0.0046, n=73/109), HELP +0.0539 (p=0.0493), SWITCH -0.0199 (p=0.6514). Quintile gaps were inconsistent in sign (-0.0440, -0.0231, +0.0138, +0.0133, +0.0966). Carryover for DROP was +0.0039 (p=0.4244). Recorded failure mechanism: E_unclear.

Within-game 'did_adapt' toward counter play types for the inferred scheme: adapters +0.0701 vs non-adapters +0.0121 (advantage about +0.058 PPP). The subgroup pattern was heterogeneous (DROP +0.1001, SWITCH -0.0436, HELP +0.0450; SWITCH reversed in [prior work]). One cut passage notes that the no-signal baseline had the highest dPPP. Recorded limit: selection or regression to the mean.

NYK vs PHI 2025-26 case study: n=8 team-game rows, adapters +0.0327 vs non-adapters -0.2987 dPPP. The A2 test could not be computed because the SHOULD vector was missing. Recorded failure type: A_unanswerable. Recorded risk: SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a positive PPP change for teams that shift toward the 'counter' play types as proof of a real coverage response
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact: the dose-response, asymmetry and carryover predictions failed. Recorded limits are selection/regression to the mean and label/classification error, with a mechanical floor.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game adapter vs non-adapter comparison of later-game PPP
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limit: selection or regression to the mean. Effects were heterogeneous by scheme, and the no-signal baseline was highest.
Recorded as inconclusive. The mechanism was unclear, and the quintile gaps did not have a consistent sign.
Recorded as untestable: n=8 and a missing SHOULD vector.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work on a closely related idea (offenses shifting toward counter play types after a defensive scheme is inferred) produced positive raw PPP gaps. [prior work] label two of the families (SF-[prior work], [prior work]) as artifacts tied to selection/regression to the mean and labelling or classification error, and the third ([prior work]) as inconclusive.
Recorded effects were heterogeneous by scheme (SWITCH often reversed). This is relevant to a 'league-wide' uniformity claim.
Small single-series designs were recorded as untestable.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests PULL_UP specifically as a counter to PNR suppression, so the exact question has not been answered.
The retrieved records do not report any unit-level share-with-positive-lift or median-lift statistic, and none calibrates a 70% / 2pp rule.
[prior work] do not show whether PULL_UP lift survives a placebo or alternative-play-type comparison, because the visible text is cut and I did not call read_family.
[prior work] do not establish that the apparent effects are zero. Artifact status means the construction was flawed, not that the real effect is null.
own_inferences: 'PNR fail' is likely defined by a low-PPP or suppressed-PNR state. Conditioning on that state creates regression-to-the-mean and mechanical-floor lift for almost any subsequent play type, PULL_UP included. A raw positive lift would therefore be weak evidence of a counter.

Per-unit lift estimates are likely very noisy. With roughly 50-150 qualifying PULL_UP possessions per team-season and a possession-level SD near 1.1 points, the SE is about 10-15pp, far larger than the 2pp median threshold. Under a true lift of 2pp, the share of units with lift>0 would be only about 55-60%, so the 70% rule would mostly fail by noise. Under a zero true effect plus selection-induced bias, the rule could be passed spuriously.
The two criteria (share>=70% and median>2pp) are not a calibrated test. They need a null distribution built from placebo play types and permutations.

The 'league-wide real counter' claim is a uniformity claim. Given the heterogeneity recorded in related families, it is probably too strong, and a hierarchical estimate of the mean and between-unit variance is more informative.

The data version matters. On 2026-05-23 the 2025-26 playoffs are partial and complete only on 2026-06-21, and playoff units would be small, so the sample must be frozen and the playoffs analysed separately.
uncertainties: The definitions of 'unit', 'lift' and 'PNR fail' are not given in the task statement.
The full text of the cut records was not read, so some details (for example T1/T2 construction) are unknown.
The reliability of the derived play-type labels (PULL_UP, PNR) is unknown. Earlier families flag label/classification error.
It is unknown how many PULL_UP possessions follow a PNR-fail state per unit.

historical_effect.explanation: Without [prior work] I might have judged the question as simply testable but underpowered. The retrieved records show that closely related 'counter after suppression' lifts were recorded as artifacts of selection/regression to the mean and labelling. The decision therefore shifts from a plain test to proceed_with_changes. The changes are a prior-possession state definition, a placebo and alternative-play-type baseline, a hierarchical estimator, and a rule calibrated against the placebo null.

blocking_constraints.text: If 'PNR fail' is defined from the PNR possession outcomes, or from the same window that scores PULL_UP, the lift is partly built into the label.
Selecting low-PNR-PPP states guarantees rebound for any following play type. Only lift above the placebo play types is interpretable.
Per-unit lift SE of about 10-15pp versus the 2pp threshold means the sign-share criterion is badly underpowered at team-season level.

prior_work.summary: The related question of whether adapting toward scheme-specific counter play types improves PPP was studied. Raw positive gaps appeared but were recorded as artifacts (SF-[prior work], [prior work]) or inconclusive ([prior work]), with heterogeneity by scheme. The PULL_UP-after-PNR-fail question with a unit-consistency rule was not directly tested in the retrieved records.

risks.text: 'PNR fail' may be defined from PNR outcomes (misses, turnovers, low PPP) that are correlated with later outcomes.
Selection on a poor-PNR state yields positive subsequent lift for every play type, which would inflate PULL_UP lift. Related families were recorded as limited by this.
Low PNR PPP means any alternative has room to exceed it. SF-[prior work] recorded MECHANICAL_FLOOR as a risk.
Per-unit noise dwarfs a 2pp effect. Playoff units and the partial 2025-26 playoff data are especially thin.
PULL_UP possessions that follow a PNR-fail state may be few per team-season.
Derived play-type labels (PULL_UP vs PNR vs others) may misclassify. SF-[prior work] recorded LABEL_ERROR.
Player quality, lineup, opponent, score, clock and shot selection (a PULL_UP taken by the best shooters) confound the lift.
A unit-level lift has low split-half reliability, so the share>0 statistic mainly reflects noise.
Variants of the PNR-fail definition, windows and unit definitions multiply forking paths. The rule has two criteria across several seasons and subsets.
League shot profiles and defensive coverages changed over 2022-26, and the regular season differs from the playoffs.
Interpretation depends on the choice of placebo or comparator play types. Related families showed that the no-signal baseline can be highest.

design.estimand: For each offense unit u, the difference in points per possession between PULL_UP possessions that occur in a pre-defined PNR-suppressed state and a matched comparator. The primary comparator is the same unit's non-PULL_UP, non-PNR half-court possessions in the same state (the placebo set). A secondary comparator is the same unit's PULL_UP PPP outside the state. The counter-specific estimand is lift_PULLUP minus mean lift of the placebo play types. The league-wide estimand is the mean and between-unit SD of this lift from a hierarchical model, plus the share of units with posterior probability of lift>0 above 0.5.
design.unit: Primary: team-season (30 teams x 4 seasons, about 120 units). Secondary: team-game within a hierarchical model. Pre-register a minimum of 40 qualifying PULL_UP possessions per unit. Units below it are pooled via shrinkage and are not counted in the share statistic.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 for the primary analysis. Playoffs are a separate exploratory stratum. Freeze the 2025-26 data at the final regular-season dump (complete from 2026-04-13) and exclude the partial 2025-26 playoffs (complete only from 2026-06-21). Hold out 2025-26 as the confirmatory season: define the state and thresholds on 2022-25, then confirm on 2025-26. 'PNR-suppressed state' must be defined using only possessions strictly prior to the target possession, for example the last k=5 opponent-defended PNR possessions with PPP below a pre-registered threshold or with a pre-registered coverage-based flag. It must not use the target possession or its outcome. Exclude garbage time and the last 24 seconds of periods. Fix k and the threshold before any analysis.
design.power: Simulation-based. Use the observed per-unit exposure and a possession-level SD of about 1.1 to compute the sign-share distribution under true lifts of 0, 2pp and 5pp, and the SE of the hierarchical mean (expected about 1-2pp over 120 units). Report the minimum detectable mean lift. If the power to distinguish a 2pp true lift from zero via the share>=70% rule is below 0.8, record the rule as not decision-grade and rely on the hierarchical mean and between-unit SD. Check split-half reliability of unit lift (odd/even games) and report it.
design.controls: Control for opponent defensive quality, ball-handler/shooter identity (player random effects), lineup, score margin, period and clock bucket, and home/away. Match PULL_UP and placebo possessions on shot clock and score state. Compare against placebo play types (ISO, spot-up, drive, etc.) in the same state. Treat regression to the mean explicitly by comparing against the same state-selection applied to randomly assigned pseudo-fail states and to the unit's rebound from a low-PPP window in non-PNR play types.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo: apply the identical state definition to other play types and require PULL_UP lift to exceed the placebo distribution (permutation p<0.05). (2) Reverse-timing test: PULL_UP lift before the fail state should be about 0. (3) Shuffle test: randomly permute state labels within unit-season to build the null for the share>=70% and median>2pp rule. (4) Dose-response: lift should rise with stricter suppression. (5) Carryover/consistency: lift should replicate between odd and even games and across seasons (2022-25 vs 2025-26). (6) Label audit: manually check a sample of 200 PNR and PULL_UP labels against play-by-play. A pattern like SF-[prior work] (no dose-response, a negative gap vs no-signal) counts as an artifact.
design.multiplicity: One primary hypothesis (counter-specific lift above placebo, hierarchical mean). The secondary criteria (share>0, median) are reported with permutation-calibrated thresholds. State the definition variants (k, threshold, window) in advance and limit them to 3. Apply Holm correction across variants and seasons, and treat playoff and heterogeneity analyses as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if all hold on the 2025-26 confirmation and the pooled analysis: (a) counter-specific lift (PULL_UP minus placebo) has a hierarchical mean >2pp with the 95% interval excluding 0; (b) share of qualified units with lift>0 is >=70% and exceeds the 95th percentile of the shuffle-null share; (c) median unit lift >2pp; (d) the reverse-timing and label-audit checks pass. Rejected if the hierarchical mean's 95% interval excludes 2pp on the low side with adequate power. Artifact if the raw lift is positive but disappears against the placebo or reverse-timing tests. Otherwise inconclusive.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the derived play-type graph as of the final 2025-26 regular-season dump (on or after 2026-04-13). Exclude the partial 2025-26 playoffs. Record file hashes, graph-build version and the labelling code version, and re-run the 2025-26 playoffs separately after 2026-06-21 as an exploratory stratum.
